summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with left-sided abdominal pain and a history of diarrhea, concerning for diverticulitis, in the setting of neutropenia due to recent Revlimid therapy for relapsed multiple myeloma. A CT scan confirmed mild diverticulitis, and he was treated with five days of IV meropenem and fluconazole, followed by oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. He was made NPO initially due to infection risk but advanced to a full diet as symptoms resolved. His neutropenia was managed with Neupogen, resulting in improved white blood cell count. His INR was supratherapeutic on admission, requiring temporary hold and subsequent dose reduction of warfarin. A new nonocclusive deep vein thrombosis in the right femoral and popliteal veins was identified, and anticoagulation was continued. Revlimid was held during hospitalization due to infection risk. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, adjusted warfarin, and home medications with follow-up arranged in hematology, rectal clinic, and anticoagulation clinic.
